summary: Documented M1-S02 (ui, scale project, build_mode design-only). Re-rendered PLAN.md and CLARIFICATIONS.md from plan.json. Minted REQ-008..REQ-010, continuing from REQ-001..REQ-007 (M1-S01): REQ-008/REQ-009 are the Enterprise and Renewal page layouts themselves (Q20, Q14, Q22, D2); REQ-010 is the Opportunity Products related-list half of requirement.md item 2, minted specifically to record - honestly, not as covered - that it is NOT satisfied by this step's artefacts (neither layout ships a relatedLists block; assumption A26). Appended 6 decisions (D-M1S02-01..06) and 3 open items (O-M1S02-01..03) to decisions.md, sourced verbatim from the runner's envelope extensions.decision_record entries that named a built element (six of the nine entries; the other three - Q19 profile fit, the Case-vs-Opportunity object note folded into D-M1S02-05, and Q re team-selling access - named no element or were folded in, per AGENT.md Step 3's rule that an entry with nothing built differently produces no separate D- row) and from artefacts/M1-S02/deploy-order.md SS0, SS3 items 2 and 4. O-M1S02-01 carries assumption A26 (the BLOCKING relatedLists retrieve), O-M1S02-02 carries assumption A25 (the unverified platform-required-field set), and O-M1S02-03 is the design question for the M1 gate: the two layouts are byte-identical because nothing in the answers differentiates Enterprise from Renewal, which admin/record-types-and-page-layouts calls a merge candidate - recorded as an open item for a human, not resolved as a decision here. Created workbook/02-page-layouts-and-lightning-pages.md (Section 2 - Page Layouts + Lightning Pages, the section Concept 2 assigns to layouts) with 2 rows (CWB-LAYOUT-001, CWB-LAYOUT-002), and appended 2 rows to workbook/99-other-configuration.md (CWB-OTHER-003 package.xml, CWB-OTHER-004 deploy-order.md - the artefact-level default per Step 4, continuing the numbering M1-S01 started). Wrote 3 rows to traceability.md: REQ-008 and REQ-009 status In UAT (tested, manual tests outstanding at the M1 gate, matching REQ-001..007's pattern); REQ-010 status In Build - explicitly not In UAT, because no artefact and no declared test in this step's acceptance_tests[] can attest to it. check_workbook.py run on both slices exactly as M1-S01's run did: workbook/02-page-layouts-and-lightning-pages.md exits 1 with 9 'Missing canonical section' issues (all other 9 sections absent from a one-section slice) and zero per-row findings; workbook/99-other-configuration.md exits 1 with 10 (the 'Other configuration' heading is not a canonical heading the parser recognises) and zero per-row findings - the same structural, not-a-defect shape M1-S01 measured. Moved M1-S02 tested -> documented via build_plan.py set-status.
confidence_rationale: Step 11 MEDIUM on two of the named conditions. First, the same one M1-S01 hit: REQ-008/REQ-009/REQ-010 had to be minted rather than read off an existing register, anchored to the clarification ids the runner's own decision_record already cites (Q20, Q14, Q22) plus decision D2 - not a freehand id. Second, an artefact (the two layout files together) could not be verified without judgment on the six-vs-nine decision_record filter: three of the runner's nine decision_record entries name no built element (Q19 profile fit, Q re team-selling access) or restate a fact D-M1S02-05 already covers, and AGENT.md Step 3 gives no numeric target - the six-decision count in this run's instructions matched exactly what 'named an element the layout actually carries' produced, and that alignment is reported rather than assumed to generalise to a future step with a different split. Two artefacts (package.xml, deploy-order.md) again fell to Step 4's artefact-level Other-configuration default, matching precedent exactly (not a fresh judgment call). Every row carries a real source_req_id and a named verification step or, for REQ-010, an explicit statement of why no verification step exists yet; every requirement the step serves has a traceability row; re-running this step's documentation pass would replace rather than duplicate every keyed row (Step 8). Neither LOW condition applies: no row was written with an empty source_req_id, and the step's test results (tests/M1-S02/results.json) were fully readable.

process_observations.observation: REQ-008 and REQ-009 each have exactly one traceability row, tied to the layout file each names, with the same verification evidence (one build-scoped checker run covers both). REQ-010 also has a row - deliberately not omitted - so the matrix's coverage line stays honest: the related-list gap is a documented, tracked requirement, not an artefact nobody wrote a requirement for.

All six decisions and all three open items this run appended trace to a specific entry in the runner's envelope (extensions.decision_record[n] or extensions.open_items_for_the_human[n]) or a specific section of deploy-order.md, the same sourcing discipline M1-S01's doc-keeper run established and this run continued rather than reinvented.

REQ-010 (the Opportunity Products related list) is minted and immediately recorded as unsatisfied - the only row in traceability.md carrying status In Build while its step is documented. A reader who scans traceability.md for 'is M1 done' and stops at row count rather than status column would miss that requirement.md item 2's product-line entry is not yet built by anything in this milestone.

The two layouts this step produced are byte-for-byte identical (decisions.md O-M1S02-03, carried from the runner's own process_observations). Nothing in this documentation pass resolves that - it is recorded as an open design question for the M1 gate, per this task's own instruction, and it sits alongside O-M1S01-03's 'not yet selectable' gap as a second reason the M1 gate should not be read as 'Enterprise and Renewal are fully differentiated and ready.'

The runner's envelope carries nine decision_record entries; six were promoted to decisions.md D-entries because each names a built layout element, and the other three (Q19 profile fit and the Q re team-selling access, both explicitly 'no element in this step'; the Case-vs-Opportunity object note, folded into D-M1S02-05 rather than duplicated) were not. AGENT.md Step 3 states the four decision kinds but not a numeric filter for which decision_record entries qualify - this run's element-named/no-element split is a judgment applied consistently across all nine, not a rule AGENT.md states verbatim, and a future step with a decision_record shaped differently should not assume the same 6-of-9 ratio.
M1-S02 is now documented; both M1 steps (M1-S01, M1-S02) have reached documented, so M1 is ready for cross-step verification.
